notes:
Top-level summary:
- Enterprise healthcare analytics vendor evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for PHI-containing workloads. Strong requirement: US-only data residency + SOC2 + audit trail to Splunk. Interested in private endpoints (no public ingress).

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-02-25: Intro call (Maya). High level requirements captured: VPC, KMS/BYOK, audit logs, SSO.
- 2026-03-02: Deep dive with SE (Julian) — network workshop. Discussed PrivateLink vs VPC peering vs Transit Gateway.
- 2026-03-04: Security team requested architecture diagram + encryption key flow.
- 2026-03-09: KMS PoC kickoff (ff_20260309_kms-poc). SE to test CMEK with AWS CloudHSM and Azure Managed HSM options.
- 2026-03-10: Legal sent DPA + data residency questions; asked for SLA for on-prem connector.

Network / deployment notes (important):
- Prefer PrivateLink endpoints into customer VPC (no public subnets). Primary ask: AWS PrivateLink, fallback to VPC peering if PrivateLink can't reach required regions.
- Firewall rules: outbound egress only to Redwood-managed IP ranges; customer will enforce strict egress allowlist on proxy. Need exact IP/CIDR list for SOC review.
- Egress controls: all egress must go through customer NAT + proxy; customer requires proof that tokens/payloads never leave approved VLANs.
- IP allowlists: security team will only accept static IPs or pinned TLS certificates. They asked for FQDN allowlist mapping if static IPs not possible.
- Route tables / TGW: customer uses Transit Gateway in account; wants recommended route table entries and cross-account role details.
- Security groups / NACLs: minimal inbound rules, deny all except PrivateLink ENIs.
- Split-horizon DNS: customer will run local resolver; needs guidance for redirecting model-serving endpoints to PrivateLink names.

KMS / encryption:
- Requirement: CMEK support + HSM-backed keys (BYOK). Must include key rotation policy and key access audit logs.
- Customer asked for offline key import procedure and FIPS-140 validation info for HSM.

Observability / audit logging:
- Must forward all request/response metadata (token usage, model id, timestamps) to customer SIEM (Splunk). Redwood to provide consumable audit stream (syslog/HTTPS).
- Retention: 90 days of raw logs, 1 year of redacted metadata acceptable. Legal to confirm.

Performance & SLOs:
- Latency target: 99p < 150ms for short prompt generation (chat assistant). Internal target 99p < 100ms if possible.
- Throughput: baseline 200 concurrent active chat sessions, burst to 500 for scheduled events.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay premium for isolation and HSM-backed keys but will ask for Optimize recommendations.

Quotes / customer language (paraphrased):
- "We cannot have PHI traverse public endpoints — must be private to our VPC."
- "We need clear proof for auditors that keys never leave our control."

Open items / next steps (short):
- Provide static IP/CIDR allowlist OR PrivateLink ENI IP ranges (Action: SE).
- Deliver network diagram with TGW / route table entries (Action: Maya + Julian).
- Run KMS PoC: validate BYOK -> CloudHSM workflow, demonstrate key rotation and audit logs (Action: SE).
- Legal to finish data residency clause tweak (Action: Customer legal).
- Schedule on-prem connector scoping call if on-prem deployment required (Action: CSM).

Internal sales notes (shorthand):
- Good ARR potential, long sales cycle because of legal & security signoffs.
- Competitive: evaluating Anthropic + in-house model hosting. Leverage Redwood's CMEK + PrivateLink play.
- Upsell path: add Optimize for batching/quantization to reduce token costs once in production.
